observation.visible_scene: A close, top-down view of pink water lilies resting on dark, still pond water. A central open bloom with a cluster of yellow stamens sits just right of center, with a pointed green bud directly in front of it; a second, partially visible pink bloom occupies the left edge. Green lily pads fill the upper area and a large rust-brown pad lies on the right. Mirror-like reflections of the petals and the green bud appear in the black water beneath the flowers. The framing and lighting are constant throughout the sampled segment.
visible_changes: Across all sampled frames the flowers, the green bud, the lily pads, and their water reflections hold the same positions, sizes, and shapes; no translation, rotation, opening/closing, or deformation is discernible.
The overall composition and crop edges remain identical, so no camera pan, tilt, or zoom is detectable from the samples.

The scene reads as an effectively static shot: the only plausible variation would be imperceptible water-surface micro-ripple in the reflections, which is not clearly resolvable between these samples.
outside_clip_unknowns: Any motion, wind, or water current occurring before t=0 or after t=3.33 s is outside this excerpt.
Whether the reflections actually shift between un-sampled instants cannot be determined.
The cause of the stillness (calm water vs. a held camera) is not shown.
uncertain_details: Sub-frame changes in the reflection or tiny lighting flicker cannot be confirmed; pixel-level differences between adjacent frames are not clearly meaningful motion.
Slight apparent differences in petal-edge highlights are consistent with a static scene rather than object movement.
